title: Compact-support composition along a proper square: closed and open normalizations
statement:
Use the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and separated finite-type $k$-schemes of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], with the ordinary pro-etale operations $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], extension by zero $j_!\dashv j^*$ along open immersions [def-weil-extension-by-zero, prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions], and the compactification-independent compact-support functors $Rf_!$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] with their composition isomorphisms $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition], all on bounded-below complexes with an etale-origin witness [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. For a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] $r$ let $\pi_r:Rr_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*$ be the proper-coincidence comparison specified by the compactification $(\mathrm{id},r)$; for an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $j$ identify $Rj_!=j_!$ by the compactification $(j,\mathrm{id})$. Consider a commutative square of separated finite-type $k$-schemes
$$\begin{array}{ccc} W&\xrightarrow{t_W}&W'\\ h\downarrow&&\downarrow h'\\ X&\xrightarrow{t}&X'\end{array},\qquad h't_W=th,$$
with $t,t_W$ proper, and define
$$\chi:Rh'_!Rt_{W*}\xrightarrow{\pi_{t_W}^{-1}}Rh'_!Rt_{W!}\xrightarrow{\alpha_{h',t_W}}R(h't_W)_!=R(th)_!\xrightarrow{\alpha_{t,h}^{-1}}Rt_!Rh_!\xrightarrow{\pi_t}Rt_*Rh_!.$$
1. If $h,h'$ are proper, then, after identifying $Rh_!=Rh_*$ and $Rh'_!=Rh'_*$ by $\pi_h,\pi_{h'}$, $\chi$ is the composite $Rh'_*Rt_{W*}\simeq R(h't_W)_*=R(th)_*\simeq Rt_*Rh_*$ of the ordinary derived direct-image composition comparisons, in the adjunction-compatible normalization of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3).
2. If $h,h'$ are open immersions and the square is Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], let $\mathrm{Ex}:h'^*Rt_*\to Rt_{W*}h^*$ be the square mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], under $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$ and $Lt_W^*\dashv Rt_{W*}$, of the inverse of the pullback comparison $h^*Lt^*\simeq Lt_W^*h'^*$ for $th=h't_W$, and put $\lambda=Rt_{W*}(u^{-1})\circ\mathrm{Ex}_{h_!}:h'^*Rt_*h_!\to Rt_{W*}h^*h_!\to Rt_{W*}$, with $u:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}h^*h_!$ the open unit. Then $\lambda$ is an isomorphism and $\chi$ is the adjunct of $\lambda^{-1}$ under $h'_!\dashv h'^*$: $\chi=\varepsilon_{h',Rt_*h_!}\circ h'_!(\lambda^{-1})$, with $\varepsilon_{h'}$ the counit.

Both are equalities of the specified natural transformations, not mere existence of isomorphisms with the same source and target.

Pro-etale form as in the construction of thm-sf-comp-composition (its proof steps 3, 5, 6) and the open-adjunction normalization of lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange.

proof.text: All calculations take place on the bounded-below etale-origin category of [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. By [thm-sf-comp-composition], compact-support functors preserve this class and their composition maps can be computed after any compactification choices. Use the explicit tower formula [lem-trf-compact-composition-tower-formula] for these computations. Its proper mates and open compositors are fixed maps, so it determines the transformation, not just its isomorphism class. The compactification comparisons are the specified coherent ones of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed].

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text: First compute $\alpha_{g,f}$ when $f,g$ are proper. In the tower formula choose $i=\mathrm{id}_Y$, $q=g$, $a=\mathrm{id}_X$, $p=f$. Then $V=X$, $b=c=\mathrm{id}_X$, $r=f$. The open comparison $\delta$ is the identity under the unit identifications by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. Its proper mate is $Rf_*\varepsilon_f\circ\eta_f Rf_*=\mathrm{id}_{Rf_*}$ by the triangle identity of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Hence the tower formula reduces to the ordinary compositor $Rg_*Rf_*\to R(gf)_*$. Thus $\pi_{gf}\alpha_{g,f}=c_{g,f}^{-1}(\pi_g\pi_f)$, where $c_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\to Rg_*Rf_*$ is [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition].

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text:
If $h,h'$ are proper, apply Step 2 to $(f,g)=(t_W,h')$ and $(h,t)$. Conjugating the definition of $\chi$ by $\pi_h,\pi_{h'}$ cancels the intermediate $\pi_{h't_W}=\pi_{th}$ and the two proper comparisons already built into $\chi$. The result is
$$c_{t,h}\circ c_{h',t_W}^{-1}:Rh'_*Rt_{W*}\longrightarrow Rt_*Rh_*.$$
The canonical ordinary compositor is the adjunction-compatible one by [fix-prop-adjunctions](3); its conjugation to the pullback compositor fixes the units and counits. This proves clause 1 without a Cartesian hypothesis on the square.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text: Now let $h,h'$ be open and the square Cartesian. To compute $\alpha_{h',t_W}$ choose the tower $i=h'$, $q=\mathrm{id}_{X'}$, $a=h$, $p=t$. The pullback $V=X\times_{X'}W'$ is identified with $W$ by the chosen Cartesian square, so $b=h$, $r=t_W$, $c=\mathrm{id}_W$. The tower formula says that $\alpha_{h',t_W}$ is $\Gamma_Q:h'_!Rt_{W*}\to Rt_*h_!$, with the indicated proper and identity-open identifications; the compositor $R\mathrm{id}_*Rt_*\simeq Rt_*$ with an identity is the identity by the unit clause of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], and $h_!\mathrm{id}_!\simeq h_!$ is the identity open compositor. For $\alpha_{t,h}$ instead choose $i=\mathrm{id}_X$, $q=t$, $a=h$, $p=\mathrm{id}_X$. Then $V=X$, $b=\mathrm{id}_X$, $r=\mathrm{id}_X$, $c=h$, and the identity-square open comparison and its mate are identities (the restriction clause of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] with $j=j'=\mathrm{id}$, and the triangle identity for $\mathrm{id}$). Both composites use the same compactification $(h,t)$ of $th=h't_W$. Consequently the explicit factors $\pi_t\alpha_{t,h}^{-1}\alpha_{h',t_W}\pi_{t_W}^{-1}$ defining $\chi$ reduce to $\Gamma_Q$, with no residual refinement automorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text:
Put $J=h_!$, $K=h^*$, $J'=h'_!$, $K'=h'^*$, $P=Lt^*$, $R=Rt_*$, $Q=Lt_W^*$ and $S=Rt_{W*}$. Let $u:1\to KJ$, $u':1\to K'J'$ be the open units, isomorphisms by [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Let $c:KP\to QK'$ be the pullback comparison. Write $\delta:PJ'\to JQ$ for the open comparison. Its restriction is the identity by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange], meaning precisely
$$K(\delta_M)=u_{QM}\circ Q((u'_M)^{-1})\circ c_{J'M}.$$
Therefore $K(\delta_M^{-1})u_{QM}=c_{J'M}^{-1}Q(u'_M)$. Hence $c^{-1}:QK'\to KP$ is the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $\delta^{-1}:JQ\to PJ'$ under $J\dashv K$, $J'\dashv K'$. Indeed, that mate has components $KP(\varepsilon'_M)\circ K(\delta^{-1}_{K'M})\circ u_{QK'M}$; substituting the displayed identity at $K'M$ turns this into $KP(\varepsilon'_M)\circ c^{-1}_{J'K'M}\circ Q(u'_{K'M})$, which by naturality of $c^{-1}$ in $\varepsilon'_M$ equals $c^{-1}_M\circ QK'(\varepsilon'_M)\circ Q(u'_{K'M})=c^{-1}_M$, by the triangle identity of $J'\dashv K'$. This is the unit equation of [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] read for $c^{-1}$. This checks the inverse direction as well as the two distinct open units.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] to $\delta^{-1}:JQ\to PJ'$: first take its mate under the two open adjunctions, which is $c^{-1}$ by Step 5, then its mate under $Q\dashv S$ and $P\dashv R$. The latter is exactly the specified $\mathrm{Ex}:K'R\to SK$ by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The iterated-mate identity identifies it with the conjugate of $\delta^{-1}$ for $PJ'\dashv K'R$ and $JQ\dashv SK$. Conjugation reverses composition and preserves identity maps [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], so this conjugate is invertible and its inverse is the conjugate of $\delta$. In particular $\mathrm{Ex}$ is invertible here because $\delta$ is an isomorphism between left adjoints; no assertion about invertibility of arbitrary square mates is used.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] in the other order to $\delta:PJ'\to JQ$. Its mate under $Q\dashv S$, $P\dashv R$ is $\Gamma_Q:J'S\to RJ$, by the explicit formula in [lem-trf-compact-composition-tower-formula]. Taking its mate under $J'\dashv K'$, $J\dashv K$ gives the conjugate of $\delta$, hence $\mathrm{Ex}^{-1}:SK\to K'R$ by Step 6. The mate-unit identity of [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] for this second mate gives
$$K'(\Gamma_{Q,N})\circ u'_{SN}=\mathrm{Ex}^{-1}_{JN}\circ S(u_N).$$
The left side is the ordinary $J'\dashv K'$ transpose of $\Gamma_{Q,N}$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), computation on trivial and Cartesian open compactification towers; Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open)

proof.text:
The open unit $u$ and $\mathrm{Ex}$ are isomorphisms (Steps 5–6). Thus $\lambda=S(u^{-1})\circ\mathrm{Ex}_J$ is invertible with
$$\lambda_N^{-1}=\mathrm{Ex}_{JN}^{-1}\circ S(u_N).$$
By Step 7 this is the transpose of $\Gamma_{Q,N}=\chi_N$ (Step 4). The inverse formula for the adjunction Hom bijection [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] therefore gives
$$\chi_N=\varepsilon_{h',Rt_*h_!N}\circ h'_!(\lambda_N^{-1}).$$
All equalities are natural in $N$ because the comparisons, units, counits and mate bijections used above are natural. This proves clause 2 as an equality of the specified natural transformations.
